features.description: Per-model canary gate: extend Executor with CanaryCheck (default no-op), implement motoko canary, hook into the EXISTING per-model agent filter at cmd/ailang/eval_suite.go:~408 (NOT next to HealthCheck, which runs per benchmark). Dead subject is skipped, banks zero rows.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately-broken motoko is skipped in <60s with reason canary_failed and ZERO result JSON files written for it
A healthy motoko passes and the suite proceeds normally
claude/codex/managed_agents unaffected via default no-op; their existing tests pass untouched
Canary runs exactly once per model per suite, asserted by a call-counter in the test
--no-canary escape hatch works
features.notes: Implemented via Go OPTIONAL-INTERFACE (executor.CanaryChecker) rather than adding CanaryCheck to the Executor interface: six executors implement Executor, and the optional pattern delivers the design's 'default no-op' with ZERO changes to the other five. Hooked into the per-model agent filter in cmd/ailang/eval_suite.go per sprint-plan C1 (NOT next to HealthCheck, which runs per benchmark). 9 tests. DEVIATION: the 'deliberately-broken motoko worktree' integration test from the plan was replaced with a hermetic registered-fake test through the real factory+resolver path — the worktree version needs mk-ast+bun+ollama, which CI lacks.

features.description: Universal Validity{Valid,Reason} on every banked result; eval_analysis excludes invalid by default with --include-invalid opt-in; quarantine the 2026-07-20 microrag_ab.jsonl row IN PLACE (never delete).
acceptance_criteria: Validity survives write->read round-trip with and without a reason
Aggregate over a fixture with one invalid row excludes it by default, includes it under --include-invalid
2026-07-20 row carries validity.valid=false reason=zero_pass_all; microRAG trend then reads -3.1/-4.8/+13.1
BACK-COMPAT: rows with NO validity field are treated as valid (absent != invalid) — dedicated test
features.notes: Validity is a POINTER (*Validity) not a value — a plain struct would decode absent as {Valid:false}, silently marking every pre-v0.31.0 row invalid and erasing all history. nil == valid, guarded by dedicated tests at BOTH the struct and loader level. LoadResults/LoadResultsFromDirs now filter by default; LoadResultsIncludingInvalid / LoadResultsFromDirsIncludingInvalid opt back in. 2026-07-20 row quarantined in place with a quarantine_note recording the root cause; microRAG trend now reads -3.1/-4.8/+13.1. 9 tests.

features.description: internal/eval_analysis/paired.go: join arms on (benchmark,lang,trial_index); McNemar over discordant pairs (exact binomial when b+c<25, else chi-sq with continuity correction); extend *_ab.jsonl with a pairs array; emit from nightly-eval.sh.
acceptance_criteria: Replaying the banked 2026-07-27 microRAG data reproduces the historical aggregate delta_pp=+13.1 EXACTLY
McNemar matches hand-computed values on >=3 fixtures including the b+c=0 degenerate case
NO p-value reported when b+c<10; output states the evidence base is too small (enforced by test)
Aggregate delta still emitted — additive change, nothing removed
Unmatched benchmarks surfaced as an explicit unpaired count, never silently dropped
features.notes: Regression anchored to REAL banked 07-27 data (168 rows distilled to testdata/): reproduces the historical delta_pp=+13.1 EXACTLY, and yields b=18 c=7, chi2=4.0, p=0.0455 — a real statistic the aggregate comparison could not produce. FOUND A PRE-EXISTING BUG: the loader's dedup key omits Trial, so a --trials 2 run silently loses half its rows (84 files -> 42) AND the surviving trial can differ between arms, wrecking the join (first replay gave delta=9.5, pairs=19, unpaired=46). Added LoadArmForPairing (no-dedup + validity-filtered) rather than changing the global dedup key, which would move every existing dashboard number — flagged for Mark as a separate decision. New `ailang eval-paired` subcommand so nightly-eval.sh banks pairs without reimplementing the join in bash (shell arithmetic is what caused the 2026-07-20 artefact). 11 tests.

features.description: Capture motoko's step-0 runtime_config_resolved (currently consumed by system_prompt_guard.go then discarded) into the result row; assert against the models.yml motoko_profile claim; mismatch => validity invalid(config_mismatch).
acceptance_criteria: A row run with motoko_profile: cloud records resolved_profile=cloud and the 4 cloud extensions
A deliberate mismatch (claim cloud, run ollama) yields config_mismatch and is excluded from aggregates
Executors that don't broadcast a resolved config are unaffected (absent => no assertion, not a failure)
features.notes: SCOPE DISCOVERY: the design assumed runtime_config_resolved already carried the profile/extensions. It did NOT — only model, step_budget, 7 env flags and system_md. So M4 needed a CROSS-REPO change: motoko now broadcasts the resolved profile (mk-ast f7bbe8d, pushed to fork). Profile only; extensions/verification would need real plumbing (cfg is not in scope at the emit site) and the profile alone catches the motivating bug. Harness side: parser -> ProviderData[resolved_profile] -> AgentBenchmarkResult.ResolvedProfile -> AssertResolvedProfile at bank time -> validity invalid(config_mismatch). Permissive both ways: absent claim or absent resolution never fails, so non-broadcasting executors are unaffected. Added Validity.Detail so a quarantined row names both sides. 10 tests.

features.description: DROPPABLE (P2). Warn at A/B setup when the control arm's historical pass rate exceeds a configurable ceiling (default 90%), since a small effect cannot be resolved there. Documented in the eval guide.
acceptance_criteria: An A/B whose control has >=90% historical rate emits a loud warning naming the ceiling problem
The haiku-fmt configuration (both arms ~96%) triggers it
Warning only — never blocks a run
features.notes: CheckHeadroom + Headroom surfaced on PairedResult and warned loudly on stderr by eval-paired (stdout stays clean JSON for banking). Ceiling 90%, advisory only — never blocks, because a regression guard on a saturated arm is legitimate. Verified against the real haiku fmt config (29/30 = 96.7% -> warns) and the real microRAG control (54/84 = 64.3% -> silent). Also warns on unpaired rows. Docs: docs/docs/guides/evaluation/measurement-contract.md. 4 tests.
